message: We’ll preserve the Azure workflow for twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers, handle bursts of twenty uploads with durable recovery, and keep your accounting system external. Let’s strengthen the existing application’s access, queue and delivery contracts; regional availability, accounting compatibility and end-to-end acceptance remain unverified before handoff.

proposal.title: Refine staff permissions, durable processing and accounting delivery
proposal.body: Preserve all components, positions, connections and existing constraints. Refine the composed invoice-workflow module rather than duplicate its internal queue, database, storage or identity resources. Included scope is staff PDF upload, asynchronous extraction, review, approval, recovery and approved accounting delivery. Provisioning or modifying the existing accounting system is outside scope. Australia East remains proposed; no deployment or compatibility is established.

next.name: Asynchronous document intake
next.requirements: Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue. Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices. A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API. Use Azure. Recommend a coherent system and the engineering choices. Ask only a small material business question when needed; do not make me configure the system.

data.label: Upload and review in browser
data.description: Existing browser used by twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; outside provisioning scope. Staff upload PDF invoices and view processing status and extraction evidence. Authorized reviewers correct and approve results. Ordinary uploaders cannot approve; the application enforces permissions on every protected server operation rather than relying on browser controls. Long-running jobs return a durable job reference and expose status without requiring the upload request to remain open.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Azure Container Apps, owning browser/API, background worker, isolated PDF/OCR parser and operating tasks/monitoring. Internal generated resources include Azure Database for PostgreSQL durable transactional queue/outbox and review state, private versioned Azure Blob Storage originals, staff sign-in, separate workload identities and regional model integration; do not provision duplicate internal services. Scope: staff PDF upload, asynchronous extraction of supplier/invoice date/total/currency with source evidence, correction and review, authorized approval, recovery and approved accounting delivery. Support twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; ordinary uploaders cannot approve. Enforce live application membership and reviewer authorization server-side; sign-in alone grants no approval permission. Accept PDFs up to 10,000,000 bytes, approximately 500 uploads daily and bursts of twenty; jobs may take several minutes without an invented completion deadline. Return durable job/status references and keep processing independent of browser connections. Persist stable invoice/job identities and exact source versions. Commit workflow state and queued work transactionally in PostgreSQL. Fence worker leases, recover stalled work, use bounded retries with backoff, and persist exhausted jobs in a visible dead-letter/recovery state with failure reasons. Authorized recovery preserves identities and history instead of creating fresh invoices. Incomplete or failed extraction stays visible for correction. Bind approval to the exact result revision and outbound payload; edits invalidate approval. Use a stable outbound operation ID and payload identity. Record delivery intent before calling accounting; uncertain outcomes are fenced for lookup/reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Accounting must independently pass normalized-action-v1, durable idempotency and uncertain-outcome acceptance; this does not prove its native API compatibility. An administrator supplies the external endpoint and credentials through protected destination configuration; keep credentials out of the diagram, browser, model input and logs. Treat originals and extracted fields as Confidential and potentially personal data. Keep documents and extracted data in Australia across processing, model inference, queues, data-bearing logs, backups and recovery copies. Australia East is proposed, not approved: verify Container Apps, PostgreSQL, Blob Storage, regional model support, quotas, private networking and processing geography. Never silently use global or cross-region inference. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days; qualify retention start, scheduled cleanup, object versions, SQL records and backup expiry without promising universal exact erasure. Keep invoice content out of routine operational logs. Parser isolation, model retention/abuse-monitoring policy, restore, alert delivery and operating ownership require qualification. Acceptance must cover denied uploader approval, burst intake, worker interruption, retry exhaustion/recovery, stale approvals, repeated delivery and lost accounting responses. The diagram and local synthetic evidence do not establish destination behavior or deployment.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without provisioning, recreation or modification. An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials through protected destination configuration; no identity or credential is invented or verified here. Receives only authorized, revision-bound approved invoice payloads through an authenticated adapter with stable operation and payload identities. Native field mapping, least-privilege access, durable destination idempotency, lookup/reconciliation and normalized-action-v1 acceptance remain unverified. Lost or ambiguous responses must enter reconciliation rather than trigger a fresh outbound operation. Its processing, storage, logging and backup locations must be qualified against Australian residency before invoice data is transferred.

edges.label: Authenticated HTTPS: upload, job status, evidence and review; reviewer-only approval
Authenticated approved payload; stable operation ID; bounded retries and uncertain-outcome reconciliation

requirementDrafts.rationale: Durable recovery prevents worker crashes and exhausted retries from losing invoices or creating new delivery identities. The PostgreSQL queue and recovery state are proposed internal engineering choices.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Use a durable job queue, stable invoice/job identity, bounded retries, a dead-letter/recovery path, approval checks and an idempotent outbound operation.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Persist workflow state and queued work transactionally with stable invoice/job identities. Bound retries, recover stalled workers and retain exhausted jobs in a visible dead-letter/recovery state. Restrict recovery to authorized operators, preserve identity and audit history, and test process interruption and retry exhaustion without losing work or bypassing approval.

requirementDrafts.rationale: An external endpoint is not a verified integration. Qualification must establish safe delivery without expanding provisioning into the client's accounting system.
requirementDrafts.basis: “The accounting system already exists. An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials; treat it as external, not a new system to provision.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Reference the existing accounting system without provisioning or modifying it. Accept administrator-supplied endpoint and credentials through protected configuration. Implement and qualify authenticated payload mapping, destination idempotency and outcome reconciliation before delivery; exclude secrets from browser responses, model inputs and logs. Accounting data handling must satisfy the existing Australian residency requirement.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Makes the stated uploader/reviewer separation explicit while preserving revision-bound approval and audit controls.
requirementUpdates.statement: Support twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers. Ordinary uploaders must not approve invoices. Enforce reviewer authorization server-side and permit accounting submission only after an authorized reviewer approves the exact result revision and outbound payload; edits invalidate approval. Retain approval and delivery history.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; ordinary uploaders cannot approve.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Records burst intake and asynchronous processing without inventing a completion-time guarantee.
requirementUpdates.statement: Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes, approximately 500 uploads per day and bursts of twenty uploads. Reject oversized input explicitly before parsing. Persist accepted jobs and expose status independently of browser connections; processing may take several minutes. Qualify burst handling, retries and worker recovery with representative PDFs; no exact completion deadline is established.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: 500 uploads per day, bursts of twenty. Jobs may take several minutes.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Preserves the no-duplicate outcome and distinguishes stable local identities from destination-side guarantees that still require qualification.
requirementUpdates.statement: Repeated delivery, bounded retries and worker recovery must not create duplicate accounting invoices. Persist stable invoice/job, outbound operation and payload identities. Require a qualified durable destination idempotency contract, reuse the same operation and payload for permitted replays, and reconcile uncertain external outcomes before another submission; recovery must not bypass approval.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Use a durable job queue, stable invoice/job identity, bounded retries, a dead-letter/recovery path, approval checks and an idempotent outbound operation.

skills.summary: Clarify outcome, users, existing systems, data ownership and constraints. Evolve the diagram incrementally. Derive functional requirements and propose measurable quality targets as assumptions needing confirmation. Compare clouds against the actual requirements; do not assume an enterprise identity provider or a vendor. Keep proposed and accepted decisions distinct.

skills.name: Security and reliability
skills.summary: Check data classification, residency, access boundaries, encryption choices, approval of automated actions, reliability and recovery. A drawn control is not enforcement evidence. Explain missing controls and tests. Propose requirements from the components and paths; mark default targets as suggestions, never existing company policy.

skills.name: Azure architecture guidance
skills.summary: Check Microsoft 365/Entra integration only when relevant to the user. Match model, retrieval, data and runtime services to requirements. Evaluate redundancy, regional availability, identity and recovery separately. The pinned Azure reliability reference specifically covers Functions and App Service; do not extend its validation claims to other services.
